beats.narration_text: Here's the wrong guess about this Skill — that Claude just fires off a reply when a demand letter shows up. It doesn't. It runs a triage — extract, cross-check, assess, recommend — and only then decides who touches the response. So: when a demand letter arrives, does Claude just reply?

beats.narration_text: Here's what a Skill actually is: a folder Claude reads before it does any work. This one is named demand-received. Inside sits one file — SKILL.md — and the whole instruction set lives there in plain English. No hidden logic, no compiled step. They optimized for read-and-edit-by-a-lawyer over anything you couldn't audit. Claude reads the file, then acts. The file is the program.

The instructions live under a Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and runs it — read the file, execute each step, return the result. Linear by default: no branching unless a step explicitly asks for it. They chose predictable over clever. The trade: you always know what it will try next; you give up on the tricks the model might have reached for on its own.

One instruction inside spells out the pipeline. Pull the letter's key fields; cross-check them against the portfolio you already have; score the merit; hand back response options with a recommendation attached. And if the assessment says this needs escalating, the Skill doesn't try to close it — it passes the ball to matter-intake or demand-intake. The output here is a decision about who touches this thing next, not the response itself.

production_viz.label: THE TRIAGE PIPELINE
production_viz.caption: the output is who touches it, not the reply

beats.narration_text: Claude isn't deciding whether to escalate — the assessment step is. When that step returns escalate, the Skill hands the letter off to matter-intake or demand-intake instead of writing the reply itself. The judgment lives in the checklist; Claude is just doing what the checklist said.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt you can paste directly into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini — no plugin required. I have an inbound demand letter I need to triage before I decide how to respond. Act as a first-pass triage layer, not my lawyer: name the fields you'd extract from the letter — sender, counterparty, product or matter, claim summary, dates, requested remedy; tell me what to cross-check those against in my own records; score the merit on your read of what I paste; hand back three response options — the safe one, the strong one, the escalate — and say which you'd pick and why; then name the exact conditions under which I should stop and route this to real outside counsel instead. Go deeper: run the same prompt against one of your own past demand letters that already got resolved, and compare the model's recommendation to what actually happened — where did it see the escalation coming, and where did it miss?
